name: KiiChain
rootCause: Cosmos EVM's StateDB tracked only an account's spendable balance, while x/staking and the staking precompile let a vesting account delegate locked coins. Delegating more than the spendable balance made the write-back in StateDB.SubBalance underflow (unchecked uint256) to ~2^256. The fix had been on main since May but shipped in v0.6.2 / v0.7.2 only on 19 Aug; the chain was still on an unpatched version. Repeated 18 times on KiiChain: 148.3M KII taken, 67.6M bridged to BNB Chain via Hyperlane and sold for ~$1.61M USDT; ~80.7M was frozen on-chain.

descriptions.text: Cosmos EVM's StateDB tracked only an account's spendable balance, while x/staking and the staking precompile let a vesting account delegate locked coins. Delegating more than the spendable balance made the write-back in StateDB.SubBalance underflow (unchecked uint256) to ~2^256. The fix had been on main since May but shipped in v0.6.2 / v0.7.2 only on 19 Aug; the chain was still on an unpatched version. Repeated 18 times on KiiChain: 148.3M KII taken, 67.6M bridged to BNB Chain via Hyperlane and sold for ~$1.61M USDT; ~80.7M was frozen on-chain.

An attacker drained 148.3 million KII, worth roughly $9.7 million at the pre-exploit price, from KiiChain through the Cosmos EVM exploit class that also hit MANTRA and TAC. A halt immobilized 54.4% on-chain, but the rest had already crossed to BNB Chain.

An attacker exploited vulnerabilities in the shared Cosmos EVM module (an arithmetic underflow in the staking precompile’s balance write-back after delegation, combined with vesting account handling and other undisclosed bugs). By creating a vesting account and deploying a contract to it, the attacker repeated the technique 18 times, draining approximately 148.3 million KII from various wallets. KiiChain halted the network at block 9355723 to stop further theft.

On 2026-08-22, KiiChain halted block production after an attacker exploited chained balance-accounting flaws in the shared Cosmos EVM module. KiiChain later reported that 148,326,583.15 KII was drained across 18 exploit sequences, with part of the funds bridged to BNB Chain through Hyperlane before the halt. KiiChain stated that the exploit combined an arithmetic underflow in the Cosmos EVM staking precompile's post-delegation balance write-back with additional balance-accounting flaws in the shared Cosmos EVM module. Public descriptions diverged on whether the exploit effectively minted unauthorized KII or only redirected existing balances from victim accounts.…

Multiple blockchains based on the Cosmos chain suffered exploits after Cosmos Labs publicly disclosed a vulnerability in the Cosmos EVM. Some have criticized Cosmos for "negligence" in their vulnerability management. KiiChain, one of the affected chains, wrote in their postmortem, "This loss was avoidable. ... Publishing a security fix in the open, before the chains running that code have been told privately and given time to patch, hands the vulnerability to anyone reading the commit. Standard responsible disclosure exists precisely to prevent this. Cosmos Labs gave no advance notice to downstream chains, did not flag the release as security critical,…
